clue.text: Fashion right now in Sussex resort

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it, so the following letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the two words supply all eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A style that is all the rage at present in a south-coast seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: WORTHING is a seaside town on the West Sussex coast of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthing is a coastal holiday town in the English county of Sussex, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Rotting produce out of sight of the house

definitions.text: out of sight of the house

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
to stage a play is to produce it

explanation.surface: Decaying fruit and vegetables kept hidden from the home.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is the theatre audience, not a home; 'produce' is a verb, not farm goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything in the wings is beyond the view of the audience, which theatre people call the house.

clue.text: Unusual dresser in street? Vast blunder!

indicators.note: a blunder is a mistake, so the letters are wrongly placed and need sorting

parts.note: all twelve letters, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone oddly clothed out in the road: what a huge mistake!
explanation.definitionFit: A transvestite wears clothing usually associated with the other sex, so is a dresser out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Bang up motorway the wrong way to Maidstone, for example

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the road's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written with the digit read as the letter I
Maidstone, in Kent, has a well-known jail

explanation.surface: Driving the wrong way up a motorway toward a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 stands in for the letter I. HM Prison Maidstone is in the county town of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang up is British slang for locking someone in a cell, the same as jailing them.

clue.text: One embraced by girl in play

indicators.note: something in play is moving about, so the letters are freely rearranged
to be embraced is to be held within someone's arms

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hugged by a young woman during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Goneril is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare. 'In play' does double duty, as definition and as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is the eldest daughter of Lear in Shakespeare's tragedy, a female character in a drama.

clue.text: To keep at home, flower is in wrong setting

indicators.note: one thing being inside another means it is placed within it
a setting holds a jewel, so the outer word acts as the mount around the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
the Tay is a Scottish river, a flow-er in crossword language

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a flower indoors, as it is badly placed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows: a river, here the Tay in Scotland. 'Wrong' is a noun, not an adjective describing the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in is to remain indoors rather than going out, a phrasal verb meaning to keep at home.

clue.text: Blithe Spirit not opening?

indicators.note: without its opening, the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a fairy is a supernatural spirit

explanation.surface: Is Noel Coward's comedy Blithe Spirit failing to get its premiere?
explanation.walkthrough: Blithe Spirit is Noel Coward's ghost comedy; the title splits into definition and wordplay. Drop F from FAIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy manner is light-hearted and carefree, matching the cheerful, unconcerned sense of blithe.

clue.text: Forerunner of a freelance storyteller

indicators.note: the answer is made of part of the following words, taken from within them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: The predecessor of an independent writer of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor comes before in a family line, so is a predecessor; forerunner is a close synonym.

clue.text: Are his patients normally given a double score?

definitions.text: Are his patients normally given a double score?

parts.words: Are his patients normally given a double score?
parts.note: surface reading: a doctor whose patients regularly receive forty points, two scores of twenty
setter's reading: twenty-twenty, the measure of normal eyesight given after an eye test

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a practitioner whose patients are routinely awarded marks twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so a double score suggests 20/20, normal vision; the professional who tests it is the OPTICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician examines eyes and measures sight, and perfect results are recorded as twenty-twenty vision.

clue.text: Dyke-builder's rubbish left out?

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter standing for left is dropped from the word

parts.note: offal can mean refuse or waste matter
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Asking whether the waste of the man who built an earthwork had been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFA was the eighth-century king of Mercia credited with Offa's Dyke, the earthwork along the English-Welsh border. Remove L from OFFAL.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa ordered the great earthen bank between England and Wales, so he is the builder of that famous dyke.

clue.text: Frost reported by garden centre — it's an old story

definitions.note: a clause, standing for the noun

parts.note: a nursery is a place selling plants

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: rime is a coating of frost; the verse word is said the same way

explanation.surface: A cold snap noted by a plant shop, dismissed as nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: Blocks are in answer order: the garden centre comes first. Frost sends solvers to the poet Robert Frost, but it is rime, a deposit of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional verses for children, like Humpty Dumpty, are tales handed down over centuries, so one is an old story.

clue.text: Exchanging punches, possibly?

parts.note: surface reading: two people trading blows in a fight
setter's reading: the Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught animal, so this is swapping such beasts

explanation.surface: Perhaps a description of a boxing match or brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A Suffolk Punch is an English breed of carthorse, so swapping punches is literally dealing in horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-trading means hard bargaining or shrewd exchange, originally the buying and selling of horses.

clue.text: Campaign endlessly for painting

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off the word

parts.note: to canvass is to campaign by seeking votes door to door

explanation.surface: Politicians campaigning ceaselessly to win support for a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last S of CANVASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil painting is often called a canvas, after the fabric it is painted on; a metonym naming the work by its material.

clue.text: Not knowing one's in a blissful state

definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the saying that ignorance is bliss, such a person is happy

explanation.surface: Someone unaware of the facts is perfectly happy as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half leans on Thomas Gray's line 'where ignorance is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking information is the plain meaning, and the proverb that unawareness brings happiness supplies the playful second sense.

clue.text: Rustic who follows poet in title

definitions.text: Rustic who follows poet in title

parts.words: Rustic who follows poet in title
parts.note: surface reading: a country person who tags along after a writer with a noble rank
setter's reading: in the name of Suppé's overture Poet and ___, the countryman comes after the poet

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin trailing behind a titled bard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' suggests a lord or earl, but it is the name of a work: Suppé's light-classical overture Poet and Peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor farm worker, the rustic who comes second in that famous overture's name.

clue.text: Needle of salt in long case

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other

parts.note: to long is to pine; 'case' marks this as the outer piece
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: A sewing needle made of salt stored in a tall clock case.
explanation.walkthrough: NaCl is sodium chloride. A needle is also a sharp rock spire, like the Needles off the Isle of Wight; 'long case' suggests a grandfather clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a tall pointed rock or peak, and such a slender spire is also called a needle.

clue.text: One arresting hot-rod driver, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that grips attention is riveting, so its source rivets
second meaning: a metalworker who hammers heated pins through plates

explanation.surface: A traffic cop pulling over a reckless driver of a modified car.
explanation.walkthrough: A hot rod suggests a souped-up car, but here it is a red-hot rivet being driven home.
explanation.definitionFit: A riveter fastens metal with heated pins, and to rivet someone's attention is to hold it fast, which is arresting.

clue.text: Bold course in swirling mist

indicators.note: swirling things whirl around, so the letters are mixed up
one element is placed inside the other

parts.note: the four letters rearranged and split around the other piece
a mode is a way or course of action

explanation.surface: A daring route taken through thick, eddying fog.
explanation.definitionFit: An immodest person is forward and shameless, which matches one sense of bold: brazen or cheeky.

clue.text: According to the book, an ancient Greek letter-opener

definitions.text: According to the book, an ancient Greek letter-opener

parts.words: According to the book, an ancient Greek letter-opener
parts.note: surface reading: a classical knife for slitting envelopes, as described in some reference
setter's reading: the book is the Bible, where Paul's epistle is opened by naming the citizens of Ephesus it is addressed to

explanation.surface: A textbook claim about a blade the old Greeks used for opening mail.
explanation.walkthrough: Ephesus was a Greek city in Asia Minor; the New Testament letter to its people is titled after them, so they open it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ephesian was an inhabitant of Ephesus, an ancient Greek city, and the Biblical epistle bears their name.

clue.text: It softens the sound under the sea, we hear

definitions.text: It softens the sound under the sea, we hear

parts.words: It softens the sound under the sea, we hear
parts.note: surface reading: something that muffles noise beneath the ocean
setter's reading: sea is said like the letter C, and the mark written under that letter makes it an s sound

explanation.surface: Something that dampens noise beneath the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The mark in French ç turns a hard C into a soft s sound; 'the sea, we hear' is the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the hook placed beneath a letter, as in façade, to show the c is pronounced soft.

clue.text: Appoint Master in Etonian reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges the members of a cabinet, so the letters are put in a new order
one element is placed inside the other

parts.note: the seven letters of the word rearranged
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is brought in during a shake-up of posts at Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: An Etonian is a pupil of Eton College, the English public school. Put M inside NOINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to name them for a post, which is a close synonym of appointing them.

clue.text: Get a metal box to hold soldiers

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a box that holds something has it inside

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Buying a metal case big enough to keep toy soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve, a crossword favourite for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to achieve or reach it, one sense of getting something.

clue.text: Planet extremely hazy and waterlogged

parts.note: the red planet

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A world described as very misty and soaked with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that is boggy and saturated, like a fen or swamp, is described as waterlogged; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: A British leader transported and guarded faraway

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is used

parts.note: first letter of the word
sent, in the sense of carried away or delighted
to mind is to look after or watch over

explanation.surface: A UK prime minister carried off under escort to some distant place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British leader' reads as the prime minister, but it only means the first letter of British. 'Faraway' describes a look, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A faraway look is a dreamy, distracted one, and someone wearing it is preoccupied and forgetful, which is the sense here.

clue.text: Celebrated dynasty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: praised in song or verse
second meaning: the Chinese ruling house of 960 to 1279, now often spelt Song

explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrated' looks like 'famous', but here it is a past participle meaning extolled.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroes whose praises are sung are celebrated, and the Sung was a Chinese imperial ruling family.

clue.text: Bones trouble one in retirement

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Aching joints bothering a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: AIL + I, then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilia are the large hip bones of the pelvis; the plural form matches the plural clue word.

clue.text: Doolittle's way of making up ground?

definitions.text: Doolittle's way of making up ground?

parts.words: Doolittle's way of making up ground?
parts.note: surface reading: how someone, perhaps the talking-to-animals doctor, catches up in a race
setter's reading: Alfred Doolittle in Pygmalion is a dustman, and rubbish dumped to build up land is his way of making ground

explanation.surface: Wondering how a character called Doolittle might catch up after falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Doolittle, Eliza's father in Shaw's Pygmalion, is a dustman (a refuse collector). 'Making up ground' means literally creating new land from waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A landfill site buries refuse in pits or hollows, raising and reclaiming the surface with tipped rubbish.

clue.text: They stimulate our defences. (not for clans sharing common ancestor)

parts.note: anti means against, not in favour of
gens is a Roman clan descended from one forebear; the plural is the same in this usage

explanation.surface: A statement about the immune system followed by a bracketed aside about families of shared descent.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is the wordplay. Strictly the Latin plural is gentes, but the setter takes gens as covering the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigens are foreign substances that provoke the body's immune response, triggering production of antibodies.
